claims.text: JMA press release, 12 September 2026, 09:30 JST (Sapporo Regional Headquarters): "十勝岳の噴火警戒レベルを２（火口周辺規制）から３（入山規制）に引上げ" (Tokachidake's volcanic alert level raised from 2, crater-vicinity restriction, to 3, mountain-entry restriction). Reason given: "８月１７日以降、山体付近を震源とする振幅の大きな火山性地震が増加" (since 17 August, large-amplitude volcanic earthquakes centered near the mountain body have increased), with elevated thermal activity continuing.

JMA's live volcanic activity status page for Tokachidake, checked 2 October 2026 (status dated from the 12 September 2026 09:30 JST bulletin with subsequent updates): Alert Level 3 (crater-vicinity warning/entry restriction) remains in effect; volcanic earthquakes have increased, with large-amplitude volcanic earthquakes occurring multiple times, indicating heightened volcanic activity; entry restrictions are in place in five municipalities in Hokkaido; people are warned to stay alert for large ejected rocks within approximately 3 km of the crater; ground deformation has continued since March and volcanic gas emissions have increased since April, meaning an eruption remains possible.

JMA's volcanic status bulletin for Tokachidake issued 9 October 2026, 16:00 JST: the crater-area warning remains at Alert Level 3 (entry restriction). No large-amplitude volcanic earthquakes (maximum amplitude 2 micrometers or more at the Iwosawa observation point) have occurred since 13 September, after a brief tremor-driven increase on 7 September; seismicity has since returned to a low level. A field observation on 8 October measured sulfur dioxide emissions at about 900 tons per day. Ground deformation indicating inflation at a somewhat deeper level near the volcano body has continued since March, and gas emissions have remained elevated since April.

JMA's volcanic warning for Tokachidake issued 16 October 2026, 10:00 JST (Sapporo Regional Meteorological Observatory), lowers the alert from Level 3 (entry restriction) to Level 2 (crater-vicinity restriction), judging that the likelihood of an eruption affecting the area within about 3km of crater 62-2 has dropped; the Level 2 warning now covers eruptions affecting roughly 1.5km of the crater, with entry restrictions remaining in Biei, Kamifurano and Shintoku (Furano and Minami-Furano no longer require special precaution). The bulletin notes large-amplitude volcanic earthquakes have not recurred since 13 September, though high crater-area temperatures, increased volcanic gas emissions, and continuing ground deformation (inflation at a somewhat deeper level) persist. Re-checked 1 November 2026: the Sapporo Regional Meteorological Observatory's latest bulletin, issued 30 October 2026, 16:00 JST, keeps the volcano at Alert Level 2 with activity levels and the explanatory text unchanged.

JMA's Tokachidake bulletin No. 35, issued 6 November 2026 at 16:00 JST (07:00 UTC), continues Alert Level 2 (crater-vicinity restriction). An eruption could affect the area within approximately 1.5 km of crater 62-2, with large ballistic rocks a hazard there and ash and small rocks potentially carried farther downwind. Elevated thermal activity persists; inflation-related ground deformation has continued since March, while increased sulfur dioxide emissions and occasional increases in seismic activity have been observed since April.

JMA's Tokachidake warning issued 16 October 2026 at 10:00 JST lowered the alert from Level 3 to Level 2 and named Biei, Kamifurano and Shintoku as the municipalities requiring crater-area precautions, including entry restrictions. It removed Furano and Minami-Furano from the municipalities requiring special precautions.

description: Volcanic unrest at Mount Tokachidake in Hokkaido prompted a Level 3 alert on 12 September 2026. JMA lowered the alert to Level 2 (crater-vicinity restriction) on 16 October and maintained it in its 6 November bulletin, warning that an eruption could affect roughly 1.5 km around crater 62-2. Crater-area precautions remain in Biei, Kamifurano and Shintoku. Elevated thermal activity, increased sulfur dioxide emissions and ground deformation continue.

impact.summary: JMA's 6 November bulletin maintains Alert Level 2 and warns of large ballistic rocks within roughly 1.5 km of crater 62-2, with ash and small rocks potentially carried farther downwind. Crater-area precautions apply to Biei, Kamifurano and Shintoku.

name: Volcanic Unrest — Mount Tokachidake, Japan

updates.text: The location label is corrected from five warning municipalities to Biei, Kamifurano and Shintoku, matching JMA's 16 October warning and current status page; this is not a new restriction change. JMA's 6 November bulletin maintains Level 2 and the approximately 1.5 km warning around crater 62-2.

JMA lowered Tokachidake's volcanic alert from Level 3 to Level 2 (crater-vicinity restriction) at 10:00 JST on 16 October, judging the risk of an eruption reaching within 3km of crater 62-2 had dropped; the narrower warning now covers about 1.5km, and entry restrictions eased to just Biei, Kamifurano and Shintoku, dropping Furano and Minami-Furano.

JMA's 9 October bulletin held Tokachidake at Alert Level 3, reporting that large-amplitude volcanic earthquakes have not recurred since 13 September (after a brief tremor-driven increase on 7 September) while sulfur dioxide emissions measured about 900 tons per day on 8 October and ground deformation continued; the exclusion zone and alert level are unchanged.
JMA raised Tokachidake's volcanic alert level from 2 to 3 (entry restriction) at 09:30 JST, citing a rise in large-amplitude volcanic earthquakes near the mountain since 17 August.
